root_cause.text: The `oplock_info` structure in the ksmbd subsystem was deallocated immediately using `kfree()` without waiting for an RCU grace period, despite being accessed concurrently under RCU read-side critical sections.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "ksmbd currently frees oplock_info immediately using kfree(), even though it is accessed under RCU read-side critical sections," and highlights that `atomic_inc_not_zero()` is called on already freed memory in `opinfo_get()`, while the patch diff replaces the direct `kfree()` in `free_opinfo` with `call_rcu(&opinfo->rcu, free_opinfo_rc

vuln_statements.explanation: This function performs direct kfree() on oplock_info structure without using kfree_rcu(). The oplock_info structure contains an rcu_head member (as shown in oplock.h), indicating it should be protected by RCU synchronization. The immediate kfree() violates RCU read-side critical section requirements, allowing concurrent readers to access freed memory.

This function triggers the unsafe deallocation when reference count reaches zero. It calls free_opinfo() (which internally uses kfree()) without any RCU grace period delay. Concurrent RCU readers may still hold references to the oplock_info structure while this deallocation occurs, leading to use-after-free vulnerabilities.
